briefContext: Agenda: confirm Zendesk renewal pain, show AI agent + self-service, quantify deflection ROI for 400-agent contact center.
transcript:
WEBVTT

00:00:05.000 --> 00:00:12.000
Sarah Chen: Thanks for joining. Before we jump in, I reviewed your Zendesk renewal notes — you mentioned 18% ticket growth and agent burnout.

00:00:13.000 --> 00:00:22.000
Mike Torres: Yeah, our BPO costs are up and first-response SLA slipped to four hours on email.

00:00:23.000 --> 00:00:35.000
Sarah Chen: Perfect. Today I'll show how a retail support lead — think Maria handling returns — and an agent, James, plus admin Priya configure routing. Does that match your personas?

00:00:36.000 --> 00:00:40.000
Mike Torres: Close enough. We have store associates and a central team.

00:00:41.000 --> 00:00:55.000
Sarah Chen: Great. Quick check — what would success look like ninety days post go-live?

00:00:56.000 --> 00:01:05.000
Mike Torres: Twenty percent deflection on order-status and return-policy questions without hurting CSAT.

00:01:06.000 --> 00:01:25.000
Sarah Chen: I'll anchor on that. Starting with Maria's portal — she sees order 8842 flagged for damaged shipment; the AI agent already suggested a replacement SKU from your catalog feed.

00:01:26.000 --> 00:01:40.000
Mike Torres: How is that different from our current bot?

00:01:41.000 --> 00:02:05.000
Sarah Chen: Fair objection — Zendesk's bot is keyword-driven. Ours uses your order API plus policy docs you uploaded last week. James can override and the note lands in the same ticket thread.

00:02:06.000 --> 00:02:20.000
Sarah Chen: Switching to admin — Priya sets business hours for APAC stores and maps escalation to your Slack channel.

00:02:21.000 --> 00:02:35.000
Mike Torres: What about Salesforce cases?

00:02:36.000 --> 00:02:55.000
Sarah Chen: Bi-directional sync — case 44102 here mirrors SFDC. For ROI, customers your size typically see six-month payback if deflection hits fifteen percent.

00:02:56.000 --> 00:03:10.000
Sarah Chen: Recap: we aligned on deflection target, showed persona-led flow, addressed Zendesk gap. Next step — technical deep dive Thursday with your CRM admin?

00:03:11.000 --> 00:03:15.000
Mike Torres: Yes, send the invite.

WEBVTT

00:00:03.000 --> 00:00:10.000
Alex Kim: Hi, I'll share my screen and walk through the product.

00:00:11.000 --> 00:00:25.000
Alex Kim: Here is the ticket list. Here is the automation builder. Here is reporting.

00:00:26.000 --> 00:00:35.000
Jordan Lee: Okay.

00:00:36.000 --> 00:00:50.000
Alex Kim: You can also use AI. Any questions?

00:00:51.000 --> 00:01:00.000
Jordan Lee: Not really.

00:01:01.000 --> 00:01:15.000
Alex Kim: Great, we can follow up later. Thanks.

WEBVTT

00:00:04.000 --> 00:00:15.000
Priya Nair: I shared a deck tailored to Helios — slide three maps your incident volume by campus.

00:00:16.000 --> 00:00:28.000
Tom Reed: We saw that. Our ServiceNow project stalled on change advisory board workflows.

00:00:29.000 --> 00:00:45.000
Priya Nair: I'll jump from slide five into the live tenant — employee Dana submits a VPN issue on mobile, technician Sam gets AI-suggested runbook steps.

00:00:46.000 --> 00:01:05.000
Tom Reed: Does this integrate with Azure AD groups?

00:01:06.000 --> 00:01:20.000
Priya Nair: Yes — SCIM provisioning. Case study on slide nine: peer hospital cut MTTR thirty-two percent.

00:01:21.000 --> 00:01:35.000
Priya Nair: Summarizing — CAB automation, employee self-service, measurable MTTR. Can we schedule a pilot scope workshop?

WEBVTT

00:00:05.000 --> 00:00:18.000
Elena Rossi: Goal today is to understand current state before any demo. What's your ticket volume by channel monthly?

00:00:19.000 --> 00:00:30.000
Chris Park: About 42k — sixty percent chat, thirty email, ten phone.

00:00:31.000 --> 00:00:45.000
Elena Rossi: Who owns the budget for tooling — you or IT?

00:00:46.000 --> 00:01:00.000
Chris Park: Shared. CFO cares about cost per contact; I care about agent retention.

00:01:01.000 --> 00:01:20.000
Elena Rossi: Incumbent is Intercom today — what breaks at scale?

00:01:21.000 --> 00:01:40.000
Chris Park: Routing is manual, no real SLA reporting, AI answers drift from policy.

00:01:41.000 --> 00:02:00.000
Elena Rossi: Pain qualification — if you fix one thing in Q3, is it deflection, quality, or supervisor visibility?

00:02:01.000 --> 00:02:15.000
Chris Park: Supervisor visibility — we can't see why escalations spike Tuesdays.

00:02:16.000 --> 00:02:35.000
Elena Rossi: Competition-wise, are you also talking to Zendesk or staying Freshworks-only evaluation?

00:02:36.000 --> 00:02:50.000
Chris Park: Zendesk quoted last week but implementation timeline scared us.

00:02:51.000 --> 00:03:05.000
Elena Rossi: I'll send a summary and propose a demo focused on supervisor analytics — sound right?

WEBVTT

00:00:02.000 --> 00:00:12.000
Sam Ortiz: Tell me about your company.

00:00:13.000 --> 00:00:22.000
Pat Nguyen: We do last-mile delivery, about 200 support tickets a day.

00:00:23.000 --> 00:00:35.000
Sam Ortiz: Cool. We have AI and omnichannel. Want a demo next week?

00:00:36.000 --> 00:00:40.000
Pat Nguyen: Sure.

WEBVTT

00:00:06.000 --> 00:00:20.000
Nadia Volkov: I'll cover data residency, encryption, and audit trails before features.

00:00:21.000 --> 00:00:35.000
Frank Muller: We cannot store PII outside EU — non-negotiable.

00:00:36.000 --> 00:00:55.000
Nadia Volkov: Understood. Frankfurt region, keys customer-managed. Here's SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 summary.

00:00:56.000 --> 00:01:15.000
Frank Muller: What about model training on our tickets?

00:01:16.000 --> 00:01:35.000
Nadia Volkov: Zero retention for training by default; contract addendum available. Objection you raised on latency — p95 under 400ms in EU.

00:01:36.000 --> 00:01:55.000
Frank Muller: Our InfoSec will still need a questionnaire.

00:01:56.000 --> 00:02:10.000
Nadia Volkov: I'll attach the SIG Lite today. Next: scoped POC with synthetic data only?

briefContext: Prospect runs 120 franchise locations; pain is franchisee support consistency.
transcript:
WEBVTT

00:00:04.000 --> 00:00:20.000
Leo Martinez: Meet franchise owner Ana in Austin — her Friday rush sees triple the 'app down' tickets. Shift lead Marco handles kitchen display errors. HQ ops manager Kim sets macros.

00:00:21.000 --> 00:00:35.000
Rita Shah: We need that franchise lens, not generic examples.

00:00:36.000 --> 00:00:55.000
Leo Martinez: Ana's ticket T-9921 shows POS sync delay; AI pulls the Austin store config, not corporate default.

00:00:56.000 --> 00:01:15.000
Leo Martinez: Marco escalates to Kim only when fryer integration fails — that's the thread we keep through reporting.

00:01:16.000 --> 00:01:30.000
Rita Shah: How fast can franchisees get answers without calling HQ?

00:01:31.000 --> 00:01:50.000
Leo Martinez: Target under two minutes for tier-one — Ana's flow shows suggested reply from franchise playbook v3.

WEBVTT

00:00:03.000 --> 00:00:15.000
Jon Reed: Quick demo today — integrations, AI, dashboards.

00:00:16.000 --> 00:00:40.000
Jon Reed: Salesforce sync, webhook events, sentiment tag on tickets.

00:00:41.000 --> 00:00:55.000
Amy Cho: What about Jira?

00:00:56.000 --> 00:01:10.000
Jon Reed: Yes, bi-directional. We're almost out of time — I'll email materials.

00:01:11.000 --> 00:01:15.000
Amy Cho: Okay thanks.

WEBVTT

00:00:05.000 --> 00:00:20.000
Hannah Lee: You're on Salesforce Service Cloud today — what's driving the look at alternatives?

00:00:21.000 --> 00:00:40.000
David Wu: License cost and slow releases. Agents hate the UI.

00:00:41.000 --> 00:01:00.000
Hannah Lee: Incumbent contract ends when, and is there a bake-off with anyone else?

00:01:01.000 --> 00:01:20.000
David Wu: March renewal. Zendesk and Freshdesk on the short list.

00:01:21.000 --> 00:01:40.000
Hannah Lee: Pain qualification — rank agent experience vs automation vs reporting.

00:01:41.000 --> 00:02:00.000
David Wu: Agent experience first, then automation. Reporting is fine enough.

00:02:01.000 --> 00:02:15.000
Hannah Lee: I'll tailor the demo to agent desktop and AI assist — agree?

briefContext: Brief asked to cover SSO, sandbox provisioning, and admin RBAC for 50 agents.
transcript:
WEBVTT

00:00:04.000 --> 00:00:15.000
Taylor Brooks: Jumping straight into the agent inbox — here's ticket routing.

00:00:16.000 --> 00:00:30.000
Casey Lin: We actually needed SSO and sandbox first per the prep doc.

00:00:31.000 --> 00:00:45.000
Taylor Brooks: Right, we can cover that later. Here's automation for password resets.

00:00:46.000 --> 00:01:00.000
Casey Lin: Our security team blocked the last vendor without SAML.

00:01:01.000 --> 00:01:20.000
Taylor Brooks: We support SAML — I'll show it if we have time. Any other questions on routing?

meetingTitle: Freshdesk demo — ticket routing & security review
briefContext: Agenda: demo ticket routing automation, walk the shared deck, and address IT security's SOC 2 question before pricing.
transcript:
WEBVTT

00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:08.000
Priyal Shah: Thanks everyone for joining — let's do quick intros before we dive in.

00:00:08.500 --> 00:00:15.000
Ravi Kumar: Happy to be here, I'll cover pricing and next steps toward the end.

00:00:15.500 --> 00:00:28.000
Meeting Room: Sounds good — on our side we're mainly evaluating ticket routing and reporting for the support org.

00:00:28.500 --> 00:00:40.000
Priyal Shah: Great, let me share my screen and walk through the deck on routing automation.

00:00:40.500 --> 00:00:55.000
Meeting Room: This is Farhan from the IT security team — before we go further, can you confirm this is SOC 2 compliant and where data is hosted?

00:00:55.500 --> 00:01:05.000
Priyal Shah: Good question — yes, SOC 2 Type II, and we support region-pinned hosting.

00:01:05.500 --> 00:01:18.000
Meeting Room: Got it, that covers my concern for now — back to you on the routing question.

00:01:18.500 --> 00:01:30.000
Ravi Kumar: On pricing, we'd size this based on agent seats plus the automation add-on.
